Q3_record_snapshot_refresh.isItTheSameOperation: No. The re-mint writes the substrate atoms Postgres; 'the record' is a different store served by a different route with a different owner. They are two steps, two instruments, two stores.

Q3_record_snapshot_refresh.whatARecordRefreshWouldHaveToDo: If the envelope/secondSource rail for this parcel turns out to be record-served, then the conflict payload would have to reach parcel_record_cell (or its companion row) or the reader's rendering field. Q4_contract_version.verdict: The writer path CAN express the A-148 conflict payload. The 1.30.0 pins are factory-side bookkeeping, not a runtime schema gate, and — decisively — NOTHING on the write path validates display_meta against the contract at all, so the 'silent drop' mechanism the brief hypothesised does not exist. The real silent-no-op risk is elsewhere (see Q4.realRisk).

whatTheWriterPathActuallyLoads.engine: @empressaio/atom-contract resolves to 1.36.0 in hauska-engine/pnpm-lock.yaml (declared and pinned across 9 manifests; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in the Cloud Build bake path). 1.36.0 is the version whose src/display/wire.ts defines SETBACK_CONFLICT_SECOND_SOURCE_TOKEN = 'setback-conflict-second-source' plus the VOCABULARY row (hauska-atom-contract @ 1668d6f, package version 1.36.0). The engine also resolves @empressaio/setback-corpus@1.2.0.
whatTheWriterPathActuallyLoads.factory: hauska-factory/package.json declares ^1.30.0; package-lock.json resolves 1.30.0; the Dockerfile sets ARG/ENV CONTRACT_VERSION=1.30.0; every cloudbuild.*.yaml pins _CONTRACT_VERSION: '1.30.0'. BUT the Dockerfile installs with `npm install --omit=dev` and copies only package.json (not the lockfile), so a fresh image build with the ^1.30.0 range resolves the latest 1.x at build time — the 1.30.0 in the lockfile is not what a Docker build necessarily installs. The value's real destination is the factory run record (runs.contract_version).

whyNoSilentDrop: There is no write-time schema validation of display_meta anywhere. packages/storage/src/pg-storage.ts writes the instance as JSONB (${this.sql.json(instance)}); the guards on the path are assertCanonicalParcelEntityId, assertPropertyWriteBoundary (identity/parcel-key only), resolveAccessPolicyOrRefuse, and (batch path) assertScopeOnAtoms — none inspects display_meta.
The symbol the factory imports as mint is `export function mint(): NodeId` in @empressaio/atom-contract src/identity/node-id.ts — a node-id minter, NOT an atom validator.

So an atom body carrying display_meta.secondSource.conflict would be written verbatim regardless of whether the process resolved 1.30.0 or 1.36.0. A 1.30.0 process would not strip the field; it simply has no vocabulary to RENDER it.
Q4_contract_version.whereTheVersionActuallyMatters: The READ/render side. The conflict sentence is a contract-provided vocabulary string (atom-contract src/display/wire.ts, consumed by engine-core/src/site-plan/setback-display.ts conflictNote/conflictNoteInput and by the surfaces). hauska-map #401 (848ec0aa, merged; its worktree reads `...(dm?.secondSource ? { secondSource: dm.secondSource } : {})` at api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts:1950 and composes setbackConflictNote from env.secondSource.conflict at src/lib/baked-facets.ts:1050), legacy-design-tools #688 (803cd0d5) and hauska-engine #442 (3726466a) are merged, so the render side is in place.
Q4_contract_version.realRisk: The no-op risk is the DATA ORIGIN, not the version. emitSetbackRule copies setbackTableRow.display_meta.second_source verbatim, and only adds `conflict` when `setbackTableRow.display_meta.second_source.conflict` is present (emit-setback-rule.ts:224-228). For Bastrop that row is built at warm time from the LIVE layer-23 per-parcel record plus the layer-83 Revisions second source by the A-148 detector in packages/adapters/src/local/setbacks/bastrop-conflict-a148.ts (shape 'stale-numeric-columns', secondSourceLabel 'One Click card') via bastrop-per-parcel-record.ts / bastrop-per-parcel-setback.ts. If the detector does not fire for 48021:34049's governing district on the day of the re-mint, the write SUCCEEDS and the surface DOES NOT CHANGE. The atomic safeguard is to run the dry leg and read the emitted atom body, not to reason about the version.

Q5_writes_and_where.whichStoreIsProduction: The atoms corpus IS the production serving store for the atom chain (retrieval-api reads it directly). The factory store is the production serving store for the record route. They are two different stores, which is why 'plus a record snapshot refresh' exists as a second sentence.

Q6_idempotence_reversibility.idempotent: Yes, at the atom level: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (atom_did) DO UPDATE, keyed on a deterministic atom DID; re-running produces the same DID and updates in place. The runner also reports skippedIdempotent, and listPropertyAtomsByParcelNodeId prefers the canonical entityId === parcelNodeId row (pickPreferredSetbackRule) among coexisting setback-rule rows.
Q6_idempotence_reversibility.rollbackTarget: NONE. There is no version or history table for property atoms on this path; the upsert OVERWRITES body, fetched_at and updated_at in place. The 2026-08-05 atom body is the only prior artifact and it is destroyed by the write. Material finding: no rollback target exists. The only recovery is re-running the previous writer at the previous engine SHA with the previous inputs (live layers at that date), which is not a rollback — it is a re-derivation against now-different live sources.
Q6_idempotence_reversibility.recommendation: Before any write, capture the live row read-only (SELECT body FROM atoms WHERE entity_type='setback-rule' AND (entity_id = '48021:34049' OR entity_id LIKE '48021:34049:%')) and keep it as the only rollback artifact that can exist.

dangers: THERE IS NO INVOCATION. Any command presented to the planner as 'the' re-mint is an invention unless it is the generic depth-warm runner. A fabricated write against a serving store is the worst outcome available here.

THE SILENT NO-OP IS REAL, but it is a DATA-ORIGIN problem, not a contract-version problem. emitSetbackRule adds `conflict` only when the resolved setback-table row already carries display_meta.second_source.conflict (emit-setback-rule.ts:224-228). For Bastrop that row is built at warm time from the live layer-23 per-parcel record by the A-148 detector (adapters/src/local/setbacks/bastrop-conflict-a148.ts). If the detector does not fire that day, the re-mint succeeds and the surface does not change.

RE-MINTING FROM THE WRONG PATH IS A REGRESSION, not a no-op. @empressaio/setback-corpus@1.2.0 contains no 'second_source' key at all. Any corpus-derived emit (the factory parcel-setback-cells lane, or any bake that resolves setbacks from the corpus) would emit an atom with NO secondSource and would DELETE the existing pre-A-148 prose confession the surfaces print today.

NO ROLLBACK TARGET. The write is an in-place upsert over body/fetched_at/updated_at with no version or history table for property atoms. The 2026-08-05 atom body is the only prior artifact and the write destroys it.

BLAST RADIUS. The two documented forms are county/city-wide: --row-id=Bastrop --city-cohort (whole cohort; Elgin's precedent processed 3,762 parcels) and bake-property-atom-county --county=48021. Both re-warm and --force-overwrite rewrites stored envelope geometry (R28 ring recompute, R30 road relabel) across the cohort. Only --parcel is bounded, and it is undocumented.

READ-PATH SPLIT CAN SWALLOW THE PAYLOAD. The conflict row rides the ENVELOPE facet from the atom's display_meta (hauska-map atom-chain-to-facets.ts:1950, baked-facets.ts:1050). But 48021's record slate includes setbackFrontFt/SideFt/RearFt/CornerFt and the setbackRules companion, served from factory parcel_record_cell/parcel_record_companion_row, whose author is @empressaio/setback-corpus (no conflict data), whose writer can only touch 'unaccounted' cells, whose reader's rendering is hardcoded null, and whose cell carries no atomDid because P-163 has not landed. If the rail in question is record-served, a perfect re-mint still shows nothing.

NO LEASE ON THE WRITING PATH. writePropertyAtomsBatch demands a HeldLease, but writePropertyAtom — the method the promote path actually calls — does not. So the re-mint would run with no mutual exclusion in the atoms store, while factory-conformant-reap (every 10 minutes) and factory-publish-gate-sched-hourly (hourly) write the factory store on a timer.

SANCTIONED RUNNER VS. AVAILABLE RUNNER. The 2026-09-12 P-169 ruling makes --apply Cloud-Run-Job-only (LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN, CLOUD_RUN_JOB). The only path that persists this atom has no Cloud Run/Cloud Build wrapper, so as things stand the write is either done from a seat (against the standing law) or a job must be built first. That is a decision for the planner, not something to improvise.

STALENESS OF THE BRIEF'S EVIDENCE. The brief's candidate instruments were read from a 2026-08-26 worktree. Against current main, the setback rail is now a held writer (F-11) and the A-148 detector now exists in @hauska-engine/adapters. Do not act on the 2026-08-26 reading.
